data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible without smuggling in induction if rationality is redefined as the strategic selection of the most falsifiable survivor to maximize error elimination, rather than as a guide to probable truth; however, this defense costs us the ability to claim that science progressively approaches truth (verisimilitude) in any meaningful sense, reducing scientific preference to a methodological gamble with no guarantee of future success.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If one insists that 'preference' implies an expectation of future success, then Popper's position collapses into hidden induction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If verisimilitude (truth-likeness) cannot be defined without probabilistic assumptions, then the cost of Popper's view is the abandonment of scientific realism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'strategic selection' argument implicitly assumes that severe past tests indicate future testability, then the circularity remains.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reframe the 'preference' not as an inductive inference about future performance (which would be forbidden), but as a non-inductive rule of method: we prefer the theory that has survived the severest tests because it is currently the best target for attempted falsification. The 'strongest case for induction' is that without assuming the future resembles the past, preference is arbitrary gambling. The 'strongest case for Popper' is that preferring the highly corroborated theory is simply preferring the one that offers the most informative potential for refutation. The surviving view is Popper's methodological rule, but the cost is accepting that 'corroboration' reports only past performance and licenses no expectation of future reliability, effectively severing the link between scientific success and truth-likeness.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
